correctness.rationale: Exact six-vertex zero-sum decomposition proves necessary/sufficient margins. Strict increase of the discrete second difference makes W have a unique zero; rational-power interval certificates and concavity at t=1 versus downward heredity at t=10 prove a continuous sign switch. Two independent kernel modes and rank 3 follow at a common zero; 640 rational identities were checked independently. The proof is analytic, not extrapolated from samples.

originality.rationale: The continuously weighted six-vertex bridge presents a proved transition between distinct first-loss modes and a simultaneous two-dimensional powered-distance kernel. The previously known unweighted barbell and ordinary-distance results do not assert or entail that varying the bridge produces such a crossing; the strongest inspected general negative-type sources only provide criteria and interval propagation. Relevant mathematical searches found no equivalent evaluated result, though nonindexed coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent material may appear under another terminology or in nonindexed publications.
The critical bridge length is shown to exist but is not uniquely classified or rigorously numerically isolated.
General finite-metric criteria could be specialized independently by others; no publication-priority certification is claimed.
